provenance.note: EVERY sentence and EVERY record in this file was invented for this measurement. No transcript of anyone appears, no line here is a real spoken sentence, and no record is a real loro record — the corpus is not in this repo and never will be. Every person, company, place and figure is fictional; the only non-fictional terms are `Deepgram`, `whisper.cpp`, `Postgres` and `MySQL`, which already appear in the public wiki as the doctrine's own worked examples.
provenance.shape: Utterances as whisper.cpp renders them: sentence case, punctuated, one to two sentences. `slice` names the loro records injected into the session the utterance was said in — the provenance the detector resolves against (`loro::SliceProvenance`), never the whole corpus.
provenance.labels: `correction` = the CEO is saying a RECORDED BELIEF is wrong and stating what is true instead, and a proposal against a NAMED record is the right outcome. `not-a-correction` = anything else: mishearings (the vocabulary desk's), questions, hedges, reports of somebody else's statement, sentences that merely share a value with a record, ambiguous references, and refs the writer cannot address.
provenance.scoring: A proposal is a TRUE POSITIVE only if the ref, the rejected side and the asserted side are ALL right. A proposal with the wrong REF scores as a false positive, not as a partial hit: the ref is what gets superseded, and a proposal against the wrong record is a corruption the CEO would have to catch by reading --dry-run bytes.
provenance.base rate: The negatives are ADVERSARIAL, not representative: the great majority carry a standalone `not` pivot on purpose, and most of them name a value that IS on one of the records. Precision measured here is therefore a LOWER bound on precision in use; recall is unaffected by the imbalance.
